title: SSC CGL — English Language | Synonyms
description: Subject-wise test on Synonyms (English Language) for SSC CGL. 20Q.
subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Find the synonym of the word 'PLUMMET'.

options.explanation: Rise means to move upwards, which is the opposite of plummet.
Ascend means to go up, which is not a synonym of plummet.
Soar means to fly high, which is not related to plummet.
Drop means to fall or descend, which is a synonym of plummet.

questions.explanation: To plummet means to fall or drop straight down at high speed. 'Drop' is the closest synonym.
questions.hint: Think of words related to falling quickly.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Find the synonym of the word 'eloquence' in the sentence: 'The speaker's eloquence captivated the entire audience, leaving them spellbound by his powerful words.'

options.explanation: Inarticulacy means the inability to express ideas clearly, which is the opposite of eloquence.
Articulacy means the ability to express ideas clearly and effectively, matching the meaning of eloquence.
Hesitation means pausing before speaking, which does not relate to eloquence.
Faltering means speaking in a hesitant or unsteady way, which is not a synonym of eloquence.

questions.explanation: Eloquence refers to fluent or persuasive speaking or writing. 'Articulacy' means the ability to express ideas clearly and effectively, making it the best synonym in this context.
questions.hint: Consider words that describe the quality of speaking well.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Find the synonym of the word 'EPHEMERAL'.

options.explanation: Permanent means lasting forever, which is the opposite of ephemeral.
Lasting means continuing for a long time, which is not a synonym of ephemeral.
Transient means lasting only for a short time, matching the meaning of ephemeral.
Eternal means lasting forever, which is the opposite of ephemeral.

questions.explanation: Ephemeral means lasting for a very short time. 'Transient' means lasting only for a short time; impermanent.
questions.hint: Think of words that describe something temporary or short-lived.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Find the synonym of the word 'assiduous' in the sentence: 'Despite the initial difficulties, her assiduous efforts eventually led to the successful completion of the complex project.'

options.explanation: Indolent means lazy, which is the opposite of assiduous.
Diligent means having or showing care and conscientiousness in one's work, matching the meaning of assiduous.
Careless means not giving enough attention, which is not a synonym of assiduous.
Hasty means done with excessive speed, which does not relate to assiduous.

questions.explanation: Assiduous means showing great care and perseverance. In the context of efforts towards a project, 'diligent' (having or showing care and conscientiousness in one's work or duties) is the closest synonym.
questions.hint: Consider words that describe hardworking and careful behavior.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Find the synonym of the word 'PRODIGAL'.

options.explanation: Frugal means spending money wisely, which is the opposite of prodigal.
Thrifty means using money carefully, which is not a synonym of prodigal.
Wasteful means spending money or resources recklessly, matching the meaning of prodigal.
Economical means using money carefully, which is not a synonym of prodigal.

questions.explanation: Prodigal means spending money or resources freely and recklessly; wastefully extravagant. 'Wasteful' is the direct synonym.
questions.hint: Think of words that describe spending money recklessly.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Find the synonym of the word 'pernicious' in the sentence: 'The new policy had a pernicious effect on the small businesses in the region, leading to several closures.'

options.explanation: Beneficial means producing good effects, which is the opposite of pernicious.
Harmless means not causing harm, which is the opposite of pernicious.
Detrimental means tending to cause harm, matching the meaning of pernicious.
Trivial means of little value or importance, which does not relate to pernicious.

questions.explanation: Pernicious means having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way. 'Detrimental' means tending to cause harm.
questions.hint: Consider words that describe something harmful or damaging.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Find the synonym of the word 'OBSEQUIOUS'.

options.explanation: Dominating means exercising control over others, which is not a synonym of obsequious.
Arrogant means having an exaggerated sense of one's own importance, which is not a synonym of obsequious.
Servile means having or showing an excessive willingness to serve or please others, matching the meaning of obsequious.
Assertive means having a confident and forceful personality, which is not a synonym of obsequious.

questions.explanation: Obsequious means obedient or attentive to an excessive or servile degree. 'Servile' means having or showing an excessive willingness to serve or please others.
questions.hint: Think of words that describe overly submissive behavior.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Find the synonym of the word 'LUGUBRIOUS'.

options.explanation: Joyful means feeling or expressing great happiness, which is the opposite of lugubrious.
Cheerful means happy and optimistic, which is the opposite of lugubrious.
Mournful means feeling or expressing sadness, grief, or regret, matching the meaning of lugubrious.
Optimistic means hopeful and confident about the future, which is not a synonym of lugubrious.

questions.explanation: Lugubrious means looking or sounding sad and dismal. 'Mournful' means feeling, expressing, or inducing sadness, grief, or regret.
questions.hint: Consider words that describe a sad or gloomy appearance.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Find the synonym of the word 'recalcitrant' in the sentence: 'The recalcitrant donkey refused to move, despite the farmer's persistent coaxing and prodding.'

options.explanation: Obedient means complying with orders or instructions, which is the opposite of recalcitrant.
Compliant means willing to agree or obey, which is not a synonym of recalcitrant.
Stubborn means having or showing dogged determination not to change one's attitude, matching the meaning of recalcitrant.
Docile means ready to accept control or instruction, which is the opposite of recalcitrant.

questions.explanation: Recalcitrant means having an obstinately uncooperative attitude towards authority or discipline. 'Stubborn' means having or showing dogged determination not to change one's attitude or position on something, especially in spite of good reasons to do so.
questions.hint: Consider words that describe someone who is resistant to authority or rules.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Find the synonym of the word 'MELLIFLUOUS'.

options.explanation: Harsh means unpleasantly rough or jarring, which is the opposite of mellifluous.
Discordant means harsh or unpleasant in sound, which is the opposite of mellifluous.
Sweet-sounding means pleasant to hear, matching the meaning of mellifluous.
Raspy means harsh-sounding, which is the opposite of mellifluous.

questions.explanation: Mellifluous means (of a voice or words) sweet or musical; pleasant to hear. 'Sweet-sounding' is the direct synonym.
questions.hint: Consider words that describe something pleasant to hear.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Find the word closest in meaning to 'LUCID'.

options.explanation: Obscure means unclear or difficult to understand.
Clear means easy to understand, matching the meaning of 'Lucid'.
Vague means unclear or imprecise.
Ambiguous means open to more than one interpretation, often unclear.

questions.explanation: Lucid means expressed clearly; easy to understand. Therefore, 'Clear' is the most appropriate synonym.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Choose the word that is most similar in meaning to 'ADMONISH'.

options.explanation: Praise means to express approval or admiration.
Commend means to praise formally or officially.
Reprimand means to rebuke someone, especially officially.
Applaud means to show approval or praise by clapping.

questions.explanation: Admonish means to warn or reprimand someone firmly. 'Reprimand' directly matches this meaning.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Select the best synonym for 'CANDID'.

options.explanation: Deceitful means deliberately misleading or dishonest.
Frank means open, honest, and direct in speech or writing.
Reserved means slow to reveal emotions or opinions.
Secretive means inclined to conceal feelings and intentions.

questions.explanation: Candid means truthful and straightforward; frank. 'Frank' is a direct synonym.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Choose the word that best expresses the meaning of the underlined word in the sentence: 'The committee found his arguments rather specious, lacking genuine substance.'

options.explanation: Valid means logically or factually sound.
Sound means in good condition; not damaged, injured, or diseased.
Plausible but false means appearing reasonable or probable but actually incorrect.
Authentic means of undisputed origin or genuine.

questions.explanation: Specious means superficially plausible, but actually wrong. It appears to be true but is misleading. 'Plausible but false' captures this nuance perfectly.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Identify the word that is most nearly the same in meaning as 'QUIESCENT'.

options.explanation: Active means engaging or ready to engage in physically energetic pursuits.
Dormant means having normal physical functions suspended or slowed down for a period of time.
Energetic means showing or involving great activity or vitality.
Restless means unable to rest or relax as a result of anxiety or boredom.

questions.explanation: Quiescent means in a state or period of inactivity or dormancy. 'Dormant' is the closest synonym.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Select the word which means the same as 'CAPRICIOUS'.

options.explanation: Consistent means acting or done in the same way over time.
Stable means firmly fixed or not likely to change.
Fickle means changing frequently, especially as regards one's loyalties or affections.
Predictable means able to be predicted; behaving in a way that is expected.

questions.explanation: Capricious means given to sudden and unaccountable changes of mood or behaviour; whimsical, fickle. 'Fickle' is the best synonym.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Find the word that is closest in meaning to 'PERNICIOUS'.

options.explanation: Beneficial means resulting in good; favourable or advantageous.
Harmless means not able or likely to cause harm.
Detrimental means tending to cause harm.
Constructive means serving a useful purpose; tending to build up.

questions.explanation: Pernicious means having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way. 'Detrimental' means causing harm or damage.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Choose the word that best expresses the meaning of the underlined word in the sentence: 'The ubiquitous presence of smartphones has transformed modern communication.'

options.explanation: Scarce means insufficient for the demand.
Pervasive means spreading widely throughout an area or group.
Limited means restricted in size, amount, or extent.
Rare means occurring infrequently or rarely.

questions.explanation: Ubiquitous means present, appearing, or found everywhere. 'Pervasive' means spreading widely throughout an area or a group of people, indicating widespread presence.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Select the word which means the same as 'PROFLIGATE'.

options.explanation: Thrifty means using money and other resources carefully and not wastefully.
Economical means giving good value or return in relation to the money, time, or effort expended.
Extravagant means lacking restraint in spending money or using resources.
Prudent means acting with or showing care and thought for the future.

questions.explanation: Profligate means recklessly extravagant or wasteful in the use of resources. 'Extravagant' is the most direct synonym.
questions.subject: ssc-english

questions.question: Identify the word that is most nearly the same in meaning as 'OBFUSCATE'.

options.explanation: Clarify means to make a statement or situation less confused and more comprehensible.
Elucidate means to make something clear; explain.
Mystify means to bewilder or perplex someone.
Simplify means to make something simpler or easier to do or understand.

questions.explanation: Obfuscate means to make something unclear, obscure, or unintelligible. 'Mystify' means to bewilder or perplex (someone) with something that is difficult to understand, thus making it unclear. The other options are antonyms.
questions.subject: ssc-english
